subject.title: Browser tool: 7 improvements from real-world automation field test

question: Which remaining browser automation slice should OpenClaw own next for the browser tool contract: state/readiness signals, model-advertised batch actions, CDP element inspection, or post-fill verification?
rationale: The already-merged selector/batch work leaves real gaps, but the next change affects model-facing browser semantics, compatibility with current ref/snapshot workflows, and security review for CDP/evaluate-style inspection.

options.title: Prioritize State Signals
options.body: Scope stale-ref, readiness, CAPTCHA, and compact action-result signals first so agents stop guessing when a new snapshot or human intervention is needed.

options.title: Advertise Batch First
options.body: Expose the already-supported batch action shape through the model-facing schema and docs before broader diagnostics.

options.title: Split Diagnostics Separately
options.body: Track CDP element inspection and post-fill verification as separate product issues with their own security and proof requirements.

recommendation.title: Prioritize State Signals
recommendation.body: Scope stale-ref, readiness, CAPTCHA, and compact action-result signals first so agents stop guessing when a new snapshot or human intervention is needed.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is about the browser plugin's public model-facing contract, and recent browser schema/actions/docs history makes this the strongest available routing candidate.
